clue.text: He represents this member of a noble group

definitions.text: He represents this member of a noble group

parts.words: He represents this member of a noble group
parts.note: He looks like the pronoun but is a chemical symbol, and the noble group is the family of inert gases in the periodic table

explanation.surface: A man stands as delegate for one of the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' reads as a man and 'noble group' as the peerage; in chemistry He is the symbol of the lightest noble gas.
explanation.definitionFit: The element with symbol He belongs to the noble gases, the unreactive column of the periodic table.

clue.text: I see you are heard in record with US philosopher

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is to be spoken and written as it sounds, text-message style

parts.note: said quickly, these words sound like four letters

explanation.surface: A recording that features an American philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'I see you are' sounds like the letters I C U R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek thinker who taught that pleasure, rightly pursued, is the highest good.

clue.text: What's more, it's a sincere conversion

indicators.note: conversion means the letters of a and sincere are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that a change of heart is genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's more' looks like a connective; read literally, an addition is what makes more.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in amount is a gain, which is what more means.

clue.text: Mother comprehends older sort of play

indicators.note: comprehends means holds within, so the word for mother wraps the shuffled letters

parts.note: mama is a word for mother

indicators.note: sort here is read as a verb, to arrange the letters of older afresh

explanation.surface: A mother understands an old-fashioned kind of drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' reorders OLDER into ELODR, which goes inside MAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensational, exaggerated stage drama is one kind of theatre piece.

clue.text: Top gear, to get off US highway

definitions.meaning: a garment worn on the top half, a jumper
to steer a car to the side of the road and stop

explanation.surface: Advice for a driver in top gear to leave an American freeway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top gear' suggests a car's highest gear; it means clothing for the top half.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted jumper is upper-body clothing, and drivers halt at the roadside by steering off the carriageway.

clue.text: Carroll's slithy invention-might appear in a 19a?

definitions.text: Carroll's slithy invention-might appear in a 19a?

parts.words: Carroll's slithy invention-might appear in a 19a?
parts.note: Humpty Dumpty explains slithy as lithe and slimy packed into one word; a case is a kind of travelling bag

explanation.surface: A Carroll coinage that could turn up in a doctor's notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Humpty Dumpty calls slithy two meanings packed into one word like a travelling bag; 19a is CASEBOOK, and a case is such a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend of two words into one, named by Carroll after a two-part travelling bag.

clue.text: Grant opponents shelter from blows here

definitions.meaning: General Lee's Confederate forces fought Ulysses Grant in the American Civil War
the side facing away from the wind, protected from gusts

explanation.surface: A recipient's adversaries take refuge from punches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows' suggests punches but means gusts of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered flank away from the wind, and the army commanded by Robert E. Lee.

clue.text: Maiden over? I can change all that

indicators.note: change means the letters of over and I can are put into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler vows to end the run of scoreless overs.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is one with no runs scored; 'Maiden' alone is the definition, a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's forename, and maiden means a girl in crosswords.

clue.text: Artist not as much upset as prince

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: less means not as much

explanation.surface: A painter less disturbed than a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LESS into SSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson's tale is of an Abyssinian prince of this name.

clue.text: You'll find one such letter in post

definitions.text: You'll find one such letter in post

parts.words: You'll find one such letter in post
parts.note: describes a mass-mailed letter of the kind that arrives with the morning mail

explanation.surface: A remark about what turns up in the morning mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter sent round to many recipients at once is called this kind of letter.

clue.text: Navy had oaken one from this quarter-deck

definitions.text: Navy had oaken one from this
definitions.meaning: the Royal Navy's march 'Heart of Oak' says its men have oaken ...
one of the four suits making up a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Sailors with oaken spirit on the quarter-deck of a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart of Oak' is the official march of Britain's Royal Navy. 'Quarter-deck' looks like part of a ship but means a quarter of a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts are one of four suits, so a quarter of the pack, and the navy song praises hearts of oak.

clue.text: Like our country, a hive, of industry?

definitions.text: Like our country, a hive, of industry?

parts.words: Like our country, a hive, of industry?
parts.note: Britain then had a female monarch, and a beehive is ruled by a female too

explanation.surface: Britain praised as a busy hive of industry.
explanation.walkthrough: When this was set, Britain was reigned over by a woman, as a beehive is.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm ruled by a female sovereign, which fitted both Elizabeth II's Britain and a colony of bees.

clue.text: One of the guard intended for Alice, for example

definitions.text: One of the guard intended for Alice, for example

parts.words: One of the guard intended for Alice, for example
parts.note: recalls A. A. Milne's poem in which Alice is marrying one of the guard at Buckingham Palace

explanation.surface: A soldier of the palace guard is meant for a girl called Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Milne's 'Buckingham Palace' the refrain runs 'Alice is marrying one of the guard', so that soldier is her husband-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: A man engaged to be married is someone's intended, as the guardsman is Alice's.

clue.text: Mount outside first three in National, so stop running

indicators.note: the word for mount goes round the outside of the letters taken from National

parts.note: to mount a play is to stage it

indicators.note: only the opening three letters of the word National are used

explanation.surface: A horse's mount fades after the first three fences in the Grand National, so it stops racing.
explanation.walkthrough: The National is Britain's Grand National steeplechase, which colours 'Mount' as a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that stagnates ceases to flow, so to stagnate is to cease running.

clue.text: Not a single female in this outfit

definitions.text: Not a single female in this outfit

parts.words: Not a single female in this outfit
parts.note: describes the clothes a bride collects for married life, after which she is no longer unwed

explanation.surface: A group or gang with no women at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a single female' reads as no women at all; it means a woman who is no longer unmarried.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen for her new married life.

clue.text: Maiden speeches, mediocre in parts

indicators.note: the letters are found partly in one word and partly in the next, spanning speeches and mediocre

explanation.surface: First speeches in Parliament that are only middling in places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden speeches' looks like one phrase, but 'Maiden' alone is the definition, a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's forename, and a maiden is a girl in crosswords.

clue.text: Yanks up and down, using this muscle

definitions.text: Yanks up and down, using this muscle

parts.words: Yanks up and down, using this muscle
parts.note: Americans ride between floors in a lift by this name, and an anatomical muscle that raises a body part shares it

explanation.surface: Someone jerks a weight up and down with a particular muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yanks' looks like a verb, jerks; it means Americans, who call a lift by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The American word for a lift, and the term for a muscle that raises part of the body.

clue.text: Good shot, Monsieur Noah

parts.note: Noah was the Ark's man, captain of the Ark

explanation.surface: A Frenchman praising a fine shot by someone named Noah.
explanation.walkthrough: Noah built and sailed the Ark, so he is the Ark's man.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled shooter is called this.

clue.text: Products, say of mine, used by crew

indicators.note: say signals that the word must be spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: products of a mine are ores, the clue's 'of mine' completing the sense

explanation.surface: Things a miner produces, put to use by a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Products ... of mine' are ORES; spoken, that matches the rowing blades a crew pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers in a boat's crew propel it with long-bladed poles.

clue.text: Seen on stage near Texas

definitions.meaning: the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical
the US state bordering Texas to the north

explanation.surface: Something watched in a theatre close to the Lone Star State.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous musical and the US state lying just north of Texas.

clue.text: Backing for show about Royal Society

indicators.note: about means the word for show surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: to reveal is to show
RS is the abbreviation for the Royal Society, Britain's scientific academy

explanation.surface: Support for an exhibition about Britain's science academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support; it means a turnaround or going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A going into reverse is a backward movement.

clue.text: Medical records — but not for ' Dr. Watson

definitions.text: Medical records — but not for ' Dr. Watson

parts.words: Medical records — but not for ' Dr. Watson
parts.note: a doctor keeps patient notes, but Watson's famous volume records Sherlock Holmes's detective work instead

explanation.surface: Dr Watson keeps no patient files.
explanation.walkthrough: Conan Doyle's last collection is 'The Case-Book of Sherlock Holmes', narrated by the doctor Watson.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's log of patients' histories, and also the title of a set of Holmes stories.

clue.text: Master has to study question endlessly

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the word for question is dropped

parts.note: a query is a question

explanation.surface: An expert must investigate a problem without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the Y from QUERY.
explanation.definitionFit: To master something is to overcome or defeat it.

clue.text: Martial expedition for this sea-raider

definitions.meaning: Martial here means of Mars: the NASA probes that landed on Mars in 1976

explanation.surface: A warlike voyage made by a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Martial' looks like warlike, fitting a raider; it means relating to Mars, home of the American space mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse plunderers of the eighth to eleventh centuries crossed the seas, and NASA's Mars landers bore the same name.

clue.text: Not necessarily kept out of the limelight, however

definitions.text: Not necessarily kept out of the limelight, however

parts.words: Not necessarily kept out of the limelight, however
parts.note: an actor placed towards the back of the stage is still lit, though the idiom means being overshadowed

explanation.surface: Someone who was not denied publicity after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Being moved to the back of the stage may still leave an actor in the light, though the figurative sense is to be overshadowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, positioned at the rear of the stage; figuratively, having one's attention stolen by another.

clue.text: Little Mary's Jabberwocky tree

definitions.meaning: Little Mary is old British slang for the stomach, from J. M. Barrie, so this is a childish word for the belly
in Carroll's poem the hero rests by a tree with this nonsense name

explanation.surface: A small girl's favourite tree from Carroll's nonsense poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mary' was early twentieth-century British slang for the stomach, after a J. M. Barrie play.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery word for the belly, which is what Little Mary meant, and the tree in Carroll's poem.

clue.text: Brewer & Co so poorly equipped?

parts.note: a brewery firm with only a single animal to pull its dray would be a very small outfit

explanation.surface: A brewing company whose kit is hopelessly inadequate.
explanation.walkthrough: Breweries traditionally delivered by horse-drawn dray; a firm with just one animal is meagre, the idiom for small and insignificant.
explanation.definitionFit: Small and meagrely provided, as in the idiom for a backwater town.

clue.text: The way 9 in form can provide diversion

definitions.text: The way 9 in form can provide diversion

parts.words: The way 9 in form can provide diversion
parts.note: 9 is the round-shaped answer at 9 across: a road of that shape lets traffic bypass a town

explanation.surface: A route of a certain shape that offers a detour.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 refers to 9 across: the road is circular in form, and diverts traffic round a town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A road encircling a town, carrying traffic away from the centre.

clue.text: In order to get top-class fur

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, the Nancy Mitford label for posh usage
sable is the prized pelt of a small mammal

explanation.surface: Doing something just to acquire luxurious fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In order to' looks like a purpose phrase, but 'In order' is the definition: in working condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in working order is fit to be put to service.
